data.name: Buraik
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Buraik means 'the illuminator'. This name is derived from the Arabic word 'buraq', which means 'light' or 'illumination'. In Islamic tradition, Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) is said to have travelled on Buraq during his Night Journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and then to heaven. This name is thus deeply spiritual and symbolizes enlightenment and guidance.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that represents guidance and enlightenment.

historical_references.context: Buraik ibn Haseebah Al-Aslami was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad. He participated in the Battle of Uhud and was one of the thirty-six who were given the title of 'the good news' by the Prophet.

historical_references.context: Buraik ibn Haseebah Al-Aslami was a participant in the Battle of Hunain, where the Muslims defeated the army of the tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif.
